questions.question: What is the capital of Spain?
questions.fact: Madrid became Spain's capital in 1561 under King Philip II. At about 650 m up, it's one of Europe's highest capitals.

questions.question: How many autonomous communities does Spain have?
questions.fact: Spain's 17 autonomous communities each have their own parliament and government.

questions.question: What are Spain's two autonomous cities in North Africa?
questions.fact: Ceuta and Melilla are the only parts of the European Union on the African mainland.

questions.question: Which river flows through Seville?
questions.fact: The Guadalquivir's name comes from Arabic "al-wādī al-kabīr", meaning "the great river".

questions.question: Which is the longest river that flows only through Spain?
questions.fact: The Ebro gave the whole Iberian Peninsula its name: the Romans called it Iberus.

questions.question: Which city is famous for the running of the bulls at San Fermín?
questions.fact: San Fermín runs from 6 to 14 July. Hemingway made it world-famous in his 1926 novel "The Sun Also Rises".

questions.question: Which Valencian festival burns giant figures every March?
questions.fact: Fallas figures, called "ninots", can be many metres tall. Each year one is saved from the fire by public vote.

questions.question: In which town is La Tomatina, the tomato fight, held?
questions.fact: La Tomatina happens on the last Wednesday of August, and over 100 tonnes of tomatoes are thrown in about an hour.

questions.question: Mallorca, Menorca and Ibiza are part of which islands?
questions.fact: Formentera, a smaller island, is part of the Balearics too. Its beaches are often compared to the Caribbean.

questions.question: What was Spain's currency before the euro?
questions.fact: The peseta was used from 1868 until 2002, when it was replaced by the euro at about 166 pesetas per euro.

questions.question: What is the name of Spain's national anthem?
questions.fact: The Marcha Real is one of the oldest national anthems in Europe, dating from the 1700s.

questions.question: What is unusual about Spain's national anthem?
options: It is only played at night
questions.fact: Spain's anthem has no official words, so at football matches fans just hum "lo lo lo" along to it.

questions.question: Which mountains separate Spain from France?
questions.fact: The tiny country of Andorra sits high in the Pyrenees between Spain and France.

questions.question: Which Madrid square has a statue of King Philip III on horseback?
questions.fact: Madrid's Plaza Mayor has been used for markets, bullfights, royal events and even executions over the centuries.

questions.question: Which square's clock do Spaniards watch at midnight on New Year's Eve?
questions.fact: At midnight on New Year's Eve, Spaniards eat 12 grapes, one for each chime of the Puerta del Sol clock.

questions.question: What is the capital of Catalonia?
questions.fact: Barcelona is Spain's second-biggest city and hosted the Olympic Games in 1992.

questions.question: What is the name of Barcelona's famous tree-lined walking street?
questions.fact: La Rambla runs about 1.2 km from Plaça de Catalunya to the old port and the Columbus monument.

questions.question: Gaudí's Park Güell is in which city?
questions.fact: Park Güell was planned as a luxury housing estate, but only two houses were built. It became a public park in 1926.

questions.question: Which city is home to the futuristic City of Arts and Sciences?
questions.fact: Valencia's City of Arts and Sciences was designed mostly by Valencian architect Santiago Calatrava and sits in an old riverbed.

questions.question: The Mezquita, a mosque-cathedral, is the great landmark of which city?
questions.fact: Córdoba's Mezquita has over 800 columns. A cathedral was built right in its middle in the 1500s.

questions.question: Which city's cathedral is the end of a famous pilgrimage to Saint James?
questions.fact: Saint James's remains are traditionally said to lie in Santiago's cathedral, which draws hundreds of thousands of pilgrims every year.

questions.question: What is the famous pilgrimage route to Santiago called?
questions.fact: To get the "Compostela" certificate, you need to walk at least the last 100 km of the Camino, or cycle 200 km.

questions.question: Which city is famous for its huge Roman aqueduct?
questions.fact: Segovia's aqueduct was built around 2,000 years ago without any mortar holding the stones together.

questions.question: Which Castilian city is completely surrounded by medieval walls?
questions.fact: Ávila's walls are about 2.5 km long, with nearly 90 towers and nine gates.

questions.question: Cuenca is famous for its…
questions.fact: Cuenca's "casas colgadas" hang over a gorge. One of them holds a museum of abstract art.

questions.question: Which city's Gothic cathedral holds the tomb of El Cid?
questions.fact: El Cid is buried in Burgos Cathedral next to his wife, Doña Jimena.

questions.question: Who was "El Cid"?
questions.fact: El Cid's real name was Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar. "Cid" comes from the Arabic "sayyid", meaning "lord".

questions.question: Which Spanish university, founded in 1218, is one of the oldest in Europe?
questions.fact: The University of Salamanca is famous for a tiny frog hidden on its carved front. Students say spotting it brings luck.

questions.question: Athletic Club is the football team of which city?
questions.fact: Athletic Club traditionally only fields players from the Basque Country or trained there, and has never been relegated.

questions.question: What is San Sebastián called in Basque?
questions.fact: San Sebastián has one of the highest numbers of Michelin stars per person in the world.

questions.question: Which region is famous for "pintxos"?
questions.fact: "Pintxo" comes from "pinchar", to pierce, because they're often held together with a cocktail stick.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain on the Spanish mainland?
questions.fact: Mulhacén, in the Sierra Nevada, is 3,479 m high. Spain's highest peak overall is Teide in Tenerife.

questions.question: Which rainy region in the northwest is part of "Green Spain"?
questions.fact: Galicia has more than 1,000 km of coastline, with fjord-like inlets called "rías".

questions.question: La Rioja is most famous for its…
questions.fact: La Rioja's Haro hosts a "Wine Battle" every June, where people soak each other with red wine.

questions.question: Which region grows most of Spain's oranges?
questions.fact: Valencian oranges are famous, but oranges were brought to Spain by the Moors, who first grew bitter ones.

questions.question: Asturias is famous for which drink, poured from high above the glass?
questions.fact: Asturian cider is poured from high above the glass ("escanciar") to add air and bubbles to it.

questions.question: Sherry comes from which Andalusian city?
questions.fact: "Sherry" is the English way of saying Jerez. The wine is aged using a special system of stacked barrels called "solera".

questions.question: What is the official palace used for state ceremonies in Madrid called?
questions.fact: Madrid's Palacio Real is one of the largest royal palaces in Europe, with over 3,000 rooms, but the King doesn't live there.

questions.question: Who is the current King of Spain?
questions.fact: Felipe VI became King in 2014, when his father, Juan Carlos I, gave up the throne.

questions.question: Who is heir to the Spanish throne?
questions.fact: Leonor was born in 2005 and has trained at Spain's army, navy and air force academies.

questions.question: Which sea is on Spain's east coast?
questions.fact: Spain's Mediterranean coasts have nicknames like Costa Brava, Costa Blanca and Costa del Sol.

questions.question: The Bay of Biscay is on which Spanish coast?
questions.fact: The Bay of Biscay is famous for rough seas. In Spanish it is the "golfo de Vizcaya", and its Spanish edge is the Cantabrian Sea.

questions.question: Which strait separates Spain from Africa?
questions.fact: At its narrowest, the Strait of Gibraltar is only about 14 km wide. On a clear day you can see Morocco from Spain.

questions.question: Gibraltar is a territory of which country?
questions.fact: Gibraltar has been British since 1713. Its famous Barbary macaques are the only wild monkeys in Europe.

questions.question: Which Spanish city hosted the 1992 World Expo?
questions.fact: Expo '92 marked 500 years since Columbus's first voyage. It was the same year as the Barcelona Olympics.

questions.question: Which circle dance is traditional in Catalonia?
questions.fact: In the sardana, dancers hold hands in a circle, and anyone can join in, young or old.

questions.question: What are "castells" in Catalonia?
questions.fact: The tallest castells reach ten levels of people. In 2010 UNESCO listed them as cultural heritage.

questions.question: At what time do Spaniards typically have dinner?
questions.fact: Spain is in the same time zone as Berlin, even though it's further west than London. That's one reason Spanish meals are late.

questions.question: What is "El Gordo"?
questions.fact: El Gordo has been drawn since 1812. Schoolchildren from San Ildefonso school sing out the winning numbers on 22 December.

questions.question: On which day do the Three Kings bring presents to Spanish children?
questions.fact: On the evening of 5 January, Spanish towns hold "cabalgatas", parades where the Three Kings throw sweets to the crowd.

questions.question: Which ring-shaped cake is eaten on Three Kings' Day?
questions.fact: A roscón de Reyes hides a small figure and a dried bean. Whoever finds the bean traditionally pays for the cake.

questions.question: "Tarta de Santiago" is an almond cake from which region?
questions.fact: Tarta de Santiago is decorated with the cross of Saint James, made by sprinkling icing sugar around a stencil.

questions.question: The spiral "ensaimada" pastry comes from…
questions.fact: The ensaimada's name comes from "saïm", Catalan for pork lard, which gives it its soft texture.

questions.question: Which city is known as "the city of three cultures" (Christian, Muslim and Jewish)?
questions.fact: Toledo was Spain's capital before Madrid, and it's famous for its swords and marzipan.

questions.question: Which language is co-official in Galicia?
questions.fact: Galician is close to Portuguese: they come from the same medieval language.

questions.question: Valencian is a variety of which language?
questions.fact: Valencian and Catalan are considered the same language, though Valencian has its own words and accent.

questions.question: Doñana National Park is famous for…
questions.fact: Doñana is one of Europe's most important wetlands, and one of the last homes of the endangered Iberian lynx.

questions.question: Which town is the southernmost point of mainland Spain?
questions.fact: Tarifa is a top windsurfing and kitesurfing spot, thanks to strong winds through the Strait of Gibraltar.

questions.question: What is Spain's high-speed train called?
questions.fact: AVE trains reach about 300 km/h. Spain has one of the longest high-speed rail networks in the world.

questions.question: Which artist has a museum in Málaga, the city where he was born?
questions.fact: Picasso was born in Málaga in 1881. You can also visit the house where he was born, in Plaza de la Merced.

questions.question: Which Madrid street is often called "Spain's Broadway" for its theatres?
questions.fact: Gran Vía was built in the early 1900s, and its Telefónica building was once one of Europe's tallest.

questions.question: Which Spanish city is home to the Alcázar palace used in "Game of Thrones"?
questions.fact: The Alcázar of Seville is still used by the Spanish royal family when they visit the city.

questions.question: The city of Las Palmas is on which Canary Island?
questions.fact: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria is often said to have one of the best climates of any city in the world.
